Findings:
[{"id":"f-exclusivity-2488a3cd","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it meets the preferred position. Section 2(a) grants a non-exclusive licence and affirmatively confirms we are \"not obligated to utilize the License\" and are free to acquire, develop or license competing software and services (subject only to not infringing TrueLink's IP and to our confidentiality obligations) — language that benefits us. The other \"exclusive\" references are neutral or in our favour: Section 8(d) is a nonexclusive licence to TrueLink of Credit Data, and Section 12's \"solely and exclusively\" wording is forum selection, not a dealing restriction. Section 3(i) (\"Client shall order TrueLink a credit report on each borrower for which an underwriting approval is requested through a System using the Interface\") is a narrow, self-triggered operational term applying only to transactions we voluntarily route through the Interface; read with Section 2(a) it leaves our procurement freedom intact and is not a requirements or sole-source covenant. Noted for awareness only, not flagged.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-a6e8577d","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or stipulated-sum provision payable by Client. Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"damages\", \"shall pay\", \"minimum\", \"late\" and \"interest\" return nothing of that character. Compensation (§5) is limited to fees for services actually requested plus stated monthly minimums during the term, with a documentation/dispute right in Client's favour, and §6 caps Hosting Services price increases for the first year and benchmarks rates to TrueLink's best customer pricing. The termination provision (§14) imposes no exit fee: Client simply gives written notice and services (and therefore fees) run to the last day of the following month — an ordinary wind-down of roughly one month's fees, comfortably inside the fallback's 3-month cap even if characterised as an exit cost. The spam covenant in §7 and §8f is a conduct restriction enforced through TrueLink's technical and equitable remedies, not a per-incident stipulated penalty. This meets the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer), so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-81a93eb2","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 2 LICENSE.","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no non-compete or field-of-use restraint on Client. Section 2(a) grants a non-exclusive licence and expressly confirms Client is free to acquire, develop, license or otherwise use competing software and services (subject only to TrueLink's IP and Client's confidentiality obligations under Section 10), which is better than the preferred position. Client's only covenants (Section 8: legal compliance, no misrepresentation of underwriting decisions, access limitation, content warranties) and the Section 7 anti-spam covenant are conduct restrictions, not restraints on the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build. The single reference to a \"Non-Competition Agreement\" (Section 8(d), p0054) operates as a limitation on TrueLink's licence to use Credit Data and therefore benefits us; its terms sit in a separate document and are noted only for diligence, not flagged here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-4c8b19a0","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 14 gives Client (and only Client) a unilateral right to terminate at will on written notice, with services running to the last day of the month following the notice month — an effective notice period of roughly 30 to 60 days, with no early-termination fee, penalty or other exit charge. That meets, and on the fee point exceeds, our preferred position (30 days' notice without penalty). TrueLink has no mid-term termination-for-convenience right: Section 13 sets a one-year term auto-renewing for successive one-year periods, and the only TrueLink exit is the mutual 30-day notice of intent not to renew at the end of a year (plus for-cause termination of Sections 2 and 3 on Client breach), so the walk-away scenario (Vendor convenience termination mid-term) does not arise. Two minor points noted but not redlined: (i) there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is immaterial here because Section 5(a) bills Hosting and Support Services monthly in arrears against invoices payable within 15 days, so no material prepayment accrues; and (ii) the end-of-term non-renewal notice is 30 days rather than the 90 days contemplated for a Vendor end-of-term exit, but that right is symmetric, applies only at expiry of a one-year term, and equally preserves our own flexibility, so it benefits us as much as TrueLink.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-5fd2088e","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right running against the Client. Searches for \"audit\", \"inspect\", \"records\", \"verif\", \"books\" and \"monitor\" return nothing, and the sections where such a right would sit are clean: § 5–6 (Compensation/Documentation and Disputes) gives the verification right to us (TrueLink must support its charges on request and we may contest them), and § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties with no examination right. The only TrueLink self-help right, § 8(f), is limited to implementing technical mechanisms on its own systems to prevent spamming, not access to or inspection of Client systems or records. No obligation on us to submit to audits therefore exists, and nothing sits in walk-away territory (no unlimited, unannounced or remote-access audit). Since the absence of any audit right is more favourable to us than the preferred position, there is nothing to limit and we should not introduce an audit right by redlining. Noted for the record: because there is no audit clause, the usual protective parameters (12-month frequency, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor-borne cost, no system access) are simply not needed; if TrueLink later proposes fee or usage verification, we would insert those limits then.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-f65d9023","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Sections 26 and 27 select California law with exclusive venue in the state or federal courts of San Luis Obispo County, California. That sits at the playbook fallback (Delaware or California law and courts) rather than the preferred New York position, but it is an accepted jurisdiction resolved in courts — there is no arbitration, and no foreign seat or venue outside the accepted list. The county-level venue (Vendor's home county rather than a neutral California forum) is a minor sub-element noted here rather than a deviation. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-657fe724","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"The only liability limitation in the Agreement (p0077, buried at the end of the Indemnity section) is one-sided: it caps TrueLink's liability at 12 months' hosting and support compensation, while Client's liability — including its broad indemnity under Section 12a — remains entirely uncapped. That is expressly walk-away territory under this rule (\"Customer's liability uncapped while Vendor's is capped\"), so it fails the fallback, which requires a mutual 12-month cap. The clause is also narrower than it appears in one respect (it only covers matters under Sections 3, 4, 7 and 11) and carves out only TrueLink's gross negligence and wilful misconduct; there is no mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages anywhere in the document (search for \"consequential\" returns nothing) and no carve-outs for confidentiality, data/security or indemnification. The redline makes the cap mutual and agreement-wide, sets the basis at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, adds the mutual consequential-damages exclusion and the standard uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirms Client's payment obligations are not \"damages\" for cap purposes.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual and agreement-wide, set it at the greater of 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, and add standard uncapped carve-outs.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-mfn-ead09424","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"The only most-favoured-nation language in the Agreement runs in our favour: TrueLink commits that Hosting Services rates will not exceed those charged to any other party (and will not increase for one year). Searches for MFN-style triggers (\"most favored\", \"no less favorable\", \"any other party\", \"match\", exclusivity) return no provision requiring the Client to extend TrueLink its best terms or to match third-party offers. This meets the preferred position of no MFN obligation on Customer, so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mincommit-43c18cdc","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 5 COMPENSATION.","rationale":"Section 5a does impose a minimum monthly fee for Hosting and Support Services, so the arrangement is not at the preferred \"usage/ordered services only\" position. It sits at the fallback, however: the term is a single 12-month period (Section 13), and Section 14 gives Client an unconditional right to terminate effective the last day of the month following notice, with a further right not to renew on 30 days' notice — so the commitment never extends beyond the current 12-month term and is exitable on short notice. There is no shortfall payment, liquidated damages or take-or-pay mechanic; Client simply pays the monthly minimum while service is live, and no volume caps are imposed on Client usage. Two points to note commercially rather than redline: the minimum amounts are left blank ($____) and should be set at or below expected usage, and Section 6 excludes the minimum monthly fees from Client's supporting-documentation and dispute rights (an invoicing/audit point handled under that rule).","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-3da2e3ca","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 7 UNSOLICITED COMMERCIAL E-MAIL.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no non-solicitation, no-hire or anti-poaching covenant binding the Client. Searches for \"solicit\", \"employ\", \"hire\", \"induce\", \"recruit\" and \"personnel\" return only the anti-spam section (§ 7 Unsolicited Commercial E-Mail) and routine references to employees in the access-restriction (§ 8(c)) and indemnity (§ 12) provisions; the Client covenants section (§ 8) and confidentiality section (§ 10) — the usual homes for such covenants — contain none. This matches our preferred position of no non-solicit binding the Customer, so no redline is warranted. Noting only that § 8(d) cross-refers to a separate Non-Competition Agreement, which is outside this document and should be reviewed separately for any personnel restrictions.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-renewal-4d0df6e1","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 13 (p0078) provides automatic renewal for successive one-year (not multi-year) terms, with either party able to prevent renewal on thirty (30) days' written notice. Both material parameters sit at the preferred position: 12-month renewal term and a 30-day (≤30) non-renewal notice window exercisable by us, well inside the fallback (≤60 days) and far from walk-away territory (>90 days or multi-year auto-renewal). Two preferred sub-elements are absent and are noted rather than flagged: there is no Vendor reminder 60 days before renewal, and no express cap on renewal price increases (lesser of CPI and 3%). Section 6 (p0047) partially mitigates the latter by freezing Hosting Services costs for the first year and imposing a most-favoured-rate commitment on TrueLink. No redline proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-addbb3a2","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 8 COVENANTS AND WARRANTIES OF CLIENT","rationale":"The only vendor warranty in the Agreement (Section 9) is a Y2K date-handling warranty. There is no warranty that the Hosting Services or Support Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, no conformance-to-documentation warranty for the Interface, no malicious-code or compliance-with-laws warranty, and no repair/re-performance/refund remedy. The hosting obligations in Section 3 are only \"reasonable commercial efforts\" commitments, not warranties with a remedy. This falls short of even the fallback (90 days software / 30 days services with remedies), so per the detection guidance the absent express warranty is a deviation and we insert the standard warranty and remedy after p0060. The general disclaimer in p0076 is acceptable as drafted because it is qualified by \"EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS AGREEMENT,\" so it does not swallow the inserted express warranty and needs no edit.","proposal":"Insert a TrueLink performance and conformance warranty with repair, replacement and refund remedies.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-assign-0ba91216","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 15 is the only assignment provision in the Agreement. It bars assignment by either party absent the other's prior written approval, with a carve-out only for assignment to a financially responsible affiliate. It therefore fails the fallback on two material terms: there is no successor/M&A carve-out permitting Client to assign to a purchaser in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and the consent standard is unqualified (no \"not to be unreasonably withheld\"), so TrueLink could block a corporate transaction at will. The clause does at least avoid walk-away territory — there is no Vendor termination or re-pricing right triggered by a Client change of control anywhere in the document (no \"change of control\" language appears), and Section 13/14 termination rights are not CoC-linked. The redline adds the affiliate/successor carve-out for Client, applies a reasonableness standard and a competitor bar to TrueLink assignments, and confirms a Client change of control is not an assignment, reaching the preferred position with the smallest workable edit.","proposal":"Widen the existing consent-free carve-out to Client affiliate and M&A successor assignments, and add reasonableness on our consent to TrueLink assignments, a competitor bar, and no TrueLink termination right on a Client change of control.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-indemn-55f24b52","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"low","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"Section 12(b) is TrueLink's only indemnity and it is confined to claims \"arising out of any breach by TrueLink of this Agreement or any failure by TrueLink in the performance of any of its obligations\" (p0075). There is no indemnity anywhere in the Agreement for third-party claims that the Interface, Hosting Services or Support Services infringe intellectual property rights — the only infringement language runs against Client (p0055 Client Content warranty, p0024, p0041). That fails even the fallback, which requires a Vendor IP indemnity with usual exclusions and remedies, and the imbalance is compounded by the broad Client indemnity in 12(a) covering Client's breach, the Web Site/Client Content and product/service injury claims. We add a TrueLink indemnity covering IP infringement, breach of law, data breach caused by TrueLink and gross negligence/wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation procedure; the Client-side indemnity is left untouched as the smallest edit reaching the preferred position.","proposal":"Insert TrueLink IP infringement indemnity with standard exclusions, remedies and 3x annual fees super-cap","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-insurance-1c661cbc","ruleId":"INSURANCE","ruleTitle":"Vendor insurance","severity":"low","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ 12 INDEMNITY.","rationale":"A full-text search for \"insurance\" returns no results and the outline contains no insurance heading; the miscellaneous provisions (Sections 13-30, ending at Force Majeure in p0097) contain no coverage requirement. ---

1. **Draft the liability cap manually.** The automated redline failed verification. Make the cap mutual and agreement-wide, set at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, add a mutual consequential-damages exclusion and standard uncapped Excluded Claims, and confirm our payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes. 3. **Issue the ownership, licence and assignment edits** — a Client-ownership paragraph with licence-back for embedded TrueLink IP and a no-joint-ownership sentence; affiliate and contractor coverage in the § 2(a) grant; and a mutual M&A successor carve-out plus reasonableness and competitor bar in § 15.
4. **Close the commercial blanks.** Set the § 5(a) monthly minimums at or below expected usage before execution, and consider whether the § 6 exclusion of minimums from our documentation and dispute rights is acceptable.
